knowledge_point.title: Calculating Vertical Asymptotes With Common Factors in the Numerator and Denominator

question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the vertical asymptotes of a rational function, we factor the numerator and denominator and cancel any common factors. Then, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x.$

Factoring the numerator and denominator and canceling any common factors, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x}{x(x-5)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{x}}{\cancel{x}(x-5)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we set the denominator equal to zero and solve for $x:$

$$
x-5=0
$$

This gives the solution $x=5$. Therefore, $x=5$ is the only vertical asymptote.

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: The function has no vertical asymptotes

$$

$$

Therefore, in ascending order, the equations of the vertical asymptotes are $x=1$ and $x=6.$
